title: Incident Response Foundations
summary: Follow a disciplined response process for an unplanned simulated event.
objectives: Define an incident and sequence a response from detection through review.
Explain why severity and escalation depend on context, safety, permission, and impact.

vocab.def: An unplanned event affecting or threatening normal operations.
A description of how serious an event is in a defined context.
Return a service or system to its expected operating state.

sections.heading: An incident has a lifecycle
sections.body: A classroom lifecycle is Detect, Record, Assess, Respond, Escalate, Restore, Verify, and Review. The order may loop as new evidence appears.

sections.heading: Priority depends on context
sections.body: A classroom scenario may define informational, warning, and critical conditions. Real teams use context, safety, permissions, and business impact rather than one universal label.

sections.heading: Escalation is a professional action
sections.body: Students should not act beyond their authorization or safety training. Knowing when to stop, record, and ask for help protects people and systems.

practice.prompt: Sequence a synthetic incident from alert through review, then mark the point where an uncertain or unsafe action must be escalated.

quiz.question: Why might an operator escalate an incident?
options: Because safety, permission, complexity, or impact requires another authority
Because every alert proves a critical failure
quiz.answer: Because safety, permission, complexity, or impact requires another authority

lab.objective: Classify and sequence a synthetic incident response without changing any real system.

reflectionPrompt: What makes escalation a responsible action instead of giving up?
